questions.q: A 1.2 kW hairdryer on 230 V. Best fuse?
questions.a: C) 13 A. I = 1200 ÷ 230 = 5.2 A, so 5 A would melt; choose 13 A.

questions.q: Mains in the UK is a.c. or d.c.?
The earth wire is connected to the...
Big question: why does a kettle need a 13 A fuse but a lamp only 3 A?
questions.a: The kettle has a much higher power, so it draws a larger current (about 10 A); the lamp draws well under 3 A.

questions.q: A heater draws 8 A from 230 V for 30 minutes. Energy transferred?
Explain why the fuse is in the live wire.
questions.a: So when it melts the appliance is disconnected from the high voltage (1); the appliance is safe to touch (1).

questions.q: A 6 Ω and 12 Ω resistor in series on 9 V. Current?
Explain how the earth wire and fuse work together to protect a person using a metal kettle with a fault. Portal response box.
questions.a: Live wire touches the metal case (1); earth wire connects case to ground with low resistance (1); large current flows to earth (1); current exceeds fuse rating (1); fuse melts, breaking the live connection (1); case is no longer live, so no shock (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first link: 'If a fault makes the live wire touch the metal case, a large current flows through the low-resistance earth wire rather than through a person.'
